summary: Cheryl A. Crowley works in Japanology. She studied under William R. LaFleur, Philip B. Yampolsky, and Ryuichi Abe.

Chi Chen Ho specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a PhD from UCLA in 2010 under Robert E. Buswell Jr., studied under traditional teacher Hsuan Hua, and served as a teaching assistant at UCLA.

Chi-chiang Huang specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD at the University of Arizona in 1986 under doctoral supervisor Jing-shen Tao, also studying under Robert M. Gimello.

Chi-wah Chan specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a PhD from UCLA in 1993, studying under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and Benjamin A. Elman, and worked as a teaching assistant at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Chie Ikeya is a scholar in history and archaeology. She earned her PhD at Cornell University in 2006, where she studied under David K. Wyatt.

Chien Y. Hsu specializes in Buddhist studies. Hsu studied under doctoral supervisors Leslie S. Kawamura (through 2011) and James B. Apple (attested 2013), as well as traditional teacher Zhenhua (attested 2013).

Chien-hsing Ho works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held a post as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Nanhua University (attested 2014) and later held a post at Academia Sinica (attested 2018).

Chih-mien Adrian Tseng specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned a PhD from McMaster University under James A. Benn, Nobuyoshi Yamabe, and Canshan Cheng, and became Assistant Professor at Fo Guang University (attested 2016).

Chijo Akamatsu (1886–1960) was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University (~1910–1913). He was appointed the first professor at Keijo Imperial University in 1927 and held a post at Yamaguchi University (~1949–1957).

Chikafumi Watanabe specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned a master's at the University of British Columbia and a PhD at the University of Calgary, studying under Leslie S. Kawamura, Ashok Aklujkar, Karin Preisendanz, A. W. Barber, and others.
Chiko Corona specializes in Buddhist studies. Corona studied under traditional teachers Kenkō Yamashita and Shohaku Okumura (attested 2010).
Chikyo Yamamoto (1913–1999) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts at Koyasan University, serving as a professor (attested 1970) and as a part-time lecturer (attested 1980).

Ching-mei Shyu specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She earned an MA at the University of Hawaii under Jan Nattier and a PhD from Cornell University in 2008 under Daniel Boucher, Jane-Marie Law, and Hubert Durt.
Chishō Namai (1947–) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served at Koyasan University as a professor (attested 1996) and later as president (attested 2008).

Chitai Takenaka (1945–) is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He completed a Master of Letters at Kyoto University in 1968, later serving as an assistant professor at Hanazono University (1979–1983) and professor at Tokoha University (attested 1989).

Chizuko Yoshimizu works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. She studied at the University of Tokyo and University of Vienna, worked at Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 1991), and became a professor at University of Tsukuba (attested 2015).
Chlodwig H. Werba is an Indologist and linguist who held posts as professor at the University of Vienna (attested 1997–2006, 2022). He also taught Vitus Angermeier.
Chogye Shabdrung (1981–) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sakya College in 2003 under Khenchen Sonam Gyatso.

Chogye Trichen Rinpoche (1920–2007) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He became the Eighteenth Chogye Trichen at Nalendra Monastery in 1928, studied under teachers including Geshe Tsechok and the 13th Dalai Lama, and taught multiple scholars.

Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche (1951–) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, founded the Rangjung Yeshe Institute in 1981, and taught numerous scholars.
